newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peru rebels ask for medicine for "wounded" - Spain.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels ask for medicine for "wounded" - Spain.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas holding at least 200 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on Wednesday asked Spain to mediate to get medical supplies inside to treat wounded people, the Spanish foreign ministry said.

"They have asked Spain to ask Peru to allow medicines in for the wounded," the chief foreign ministry spokesman told Reuters. There was no immediate explanation of who was wounded or how serious their condition was.

No injuries to hostages have been reported since the start of the attack, but one guerrilla of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) was shot in the leg during the initial assault on Tuesday evening.
At about 9 a.m. (1400 GMT), a large explosion was heard at the residence, where the heavily-armed rebels were holding the hostages, who include high-ranking foreign diplomats.
Smoke could be seen above the building's 10-metre (30-foot) perimeter wall and shots were heard seconds later, according to eyewitnesses.

Earlier Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar telephoned Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and asked him to avoid using military force to end the siege for fear this would lead to a massacre, Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said.
